skipped_already_reported: payment-application add_change_order forges SOV without CO approval
Curated budget-variance-analyzer use_contingency no pool erases overrun

near_misses.why: Monthly income inflates but end retainage release also goes negative; lifetime net largely cancels — weaker complete cash-theft chain than pay-app retainage
Caller-supplied path with no remote ingress; operator-controlled write only

findings.title: approve_change_order forges arbitrary APPROVED amount from DRAFT with $0 proposed — revised contract +$5M
findings.description: ChangeOrderManager.approve_change_order never checks status (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/REJECTED) and trusts caller-supplied approved_amount. An empty DRAFT CO with proposed_amount=0 can be stamped APPROVED for any dollar/time value. get_summary() then adds approved_amount into total_approved and revised_contract.
findings.impact: Attacker/agent forges a $5M executed change on a $2M contract (revised_contract=$7M) with no pricing, review, or line items. Downstream pay apps/SOV imports that trust revised_contract pay out inflated contract value.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent runs ChangeOrderManager as contract change system of record.
2. Attacker creates CO via create_change_order (status=DRAFT, proposed_amount=0).
3. Attacker calls approve_change_order(co_id, approved_amount=5000000, approved_time=90) — no status gate.
4. get_summary()/generate_log show Approved Changes $5M and Revised Contract original+$5M.
5. Subsequent billing/CO logs treat the forged approval as authoritative.
findings.remediation: Require status in SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW/NEGOTIATING before approve; bind approved_amount to proposed_amount (±tolerance) or require dual control; block re-approve of already APPROVED/EXECUTED/REJECTED; log approver identity with non-spoofable auth.

findings.title: approve_change_order skips PENDING_REVIEW/PENDING_APPROVAL — DRAFT→APPROVED status-machine bypass
findings.description: submit_for_review and submit_for_approval enforce DRAFT→PENDING_REVIEW→PENDING_APPROVAL, but approve_change_order has no status precondition. Any DRAFT (or REJECTED) CO can jump straight to APPROVED; get_summary includes total_cost in approved_changes/current_contract.
findings.impact: PoC: $100×$5000 labor +15% markup (~$695k) approved from DRAFT without reviewer step; current_contract jumps $1M→$1.70M. Distinct from already-reported add_cost_item-after-APPROVED (this bypasses the gate before approval).
findings.attack_path:
1. create_change_order leaves status=DRAFT.
2. add_cost_item loads inflated quantities/unit costs.
3. Skip submit_for_review/submit_for_approval.
4. approve_change_order(approver='attacker') sets APPROVED.
5. get_summary() reports approved_changes and inflated current_contract.
findings.remediation: In approve_change_order require status==PENDING_APPROVAL (and reject REJECTED/APPROVED). Keep add_cost_item blocked once past DRAFT. Require authenticated approver role.

findings.title: set_retainage_rates(negative) turns retainage into a credit — $500k work yields $750k net due
findings.description: set_retainage_rates assigns work_rate/stored_rate with no range check. _calculate_totals multiplies completed work by the rate, so a negative rate produces negative retainage and increases net_amount_due above total_completed.
findings.impact: PoC: work_rate=-0.50 on $500k completed → retainage=-$250k → net_amount_due=$750k (150% of earned). Owner pays a retainage 'credit' instead of holding funds.
findings.attack_path:
1. Processor initialized for project with SOV.
2. Attacker calls set_retainage_rates(-0.50).
3. create_pay_app + update_line_item bills full scheduled value.
4. _calculate_totals computes negative retainage; net_amount_due = completed - (negative retainage).
5. approve_pay_app/record_payment/G702 pay the inflated net.
findings.remediation: Clamp retainage rates to [0, 1] (or contract max). Reject negative stored/work rates. Assert retainage >= 0 and net_amount_due <= total_completed in _calculate_totals.

findings.title: approve_pay_app trusts caller approved_amount and has no status gate — DRAFT→APPROVED $9M forge
findings.description: approve_pay_app never requires SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW and sets approved_amount to the caller value whenever it is truthy, ignoring net_amount_due. record_payment similarly lacks an APPROVED precondition (DRAFT with approved_amount=0 marks PAID for any paid_amount>=0).
findings.impact: PoC: $10k progress (net=$9k) approved for $9,000,000 from DRAFT. Payment systems that disburse approved_amount overpay by orders of magnitude.
findings.attack_path:
1. create_pay_app + update_line_item for small progress.
2. Skip submit_pay_app.
3. approve_pay_app(app, approved_amount=9000000) from DRAFT.
4. Downstream pays approved_amount or G702 current due after further mutation.
findings.remediation: Require status in SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW before approve. Default approved_amount to net_amount_due; allow reductions only with recorded reason; reject increases above net. Require APPROVED before record_payment.

findings.title: update_line_item allows unbounded overbilling and mutates totals after APPROVED
findings.description: update_line_item writes current_completed/materials_stored with no cap to scheduled_value and no status lock. Billing can exceed 100% SOV (balance_to_finish goes negative). After APPROVED, the same call recalculates net_amount_due and G702 current_payment_due while approved_amount stays frozen — forms and nets diverge upward.
findings.impact: PoC: $100k SOV billed at $250k → net=$225k. Second PoC: approve at $9k then update to 100% → G702 current_payment_due=$90k while still APPROVED.
findings.attack_path:
1. create_pay_app for SOV line scheduled_value=100000.
2. update_line_item(..., current_completed=250000) — no ceiling.
3. Or: submit+approve small amount, then update_line_item to full/over value.
4. generate_g702 emits inflated current_payment_due under APPROVED status.
findings.remediation: Reject updates when status not DRAFT. Cap previous+current+stored <= scheduled_value (unless change order adjusted SOV). Freeze line items on APPROVED/PAID.

findings.title: release_retention accepts negative amount — inflate balance_held then pay out $70k on $20k retained
findings.description: release_retention only caps amount when amount > balance_held. Negative amounts pass, subtract from total_released, and add to balance_held. A follow-up positive release then pays the inflated balance. Cash systems that disburse each positive release.amount overpay retainage.
findings.impact: PoC: $20k held → release(-50000) → held=$70k → release($70k). Positive payouts sum to $70k against $20k actually retained.
findings.attack_path:
1. record_billing creates $20k retention on $200k gross @10%.
2. release_retention(..., amount=-50000) — no lower bound.
3. balance_held becomes $70k; total_released decreases.
4. release_retention(..., amount=70000) records a $70k positive release paid to the sub.
findings.remediation: Require amount > 0 and amount <= balance_held. Reject negative/NaN. Recompute balance_held as total_retained - total_released after each mutation; refuse release if balance would go inconsistent.

findings.title: release_retention ignores check_release_conditions and lien_waivers/consent flags
findings.description: check_release_conditions reports ready_for_release=False until punch list, final lien waiver, surety consent, as-builts, etc. release_retention never calls that check and stores lien_waivers_received/consent_of_surety without gating. Empty approved_by is accepted.
findings.impact: Full or partial retainage can be released while documentation and lien/surety conditions remain unmet — converting held contract security into cash prematurely.
findings.attack_path:
1. record_billing builds balance_held.
2. check_release_conditions → ready_for_release=False, many missing_conditions.
3. release_retention(..., lien_waivers=False, consent_of_surety=False, approved_by='') still releases cash.
4. Sub receives retention without closeout/lien protection.
findings.remediation: Gate release_retention on check_release_conditions()['ready_for_release'] (or explicit waiver of named conditions with audit). Require lien_waivers_received and consent_of_surety true for final release. Require authenticated approver.

findings.title: record_invoice uncapped vs contract and record_payment skips APPROVED — $450k PAID on $100k subcontract
findings.description: record_invoice never compares gross_amount to contract_amount/balance_remaining. record_payment sets PAID without requiring APPROVED (approve_payment is optional). total_paid sums PAID amounts, so over-invoicing becomes overpayment.
findings.impact: PoC: $500k gross on $100k contract → net $450k at 10% retention → record_payment → status=PAID, total_paid=$450k (4.5× contract).
findings.attack_path:
1. add_subcontractor(contract_amount=100000).
2. record_invoice(gross_amount=500000) — no cap.
3. Skip approve_payment.
4. record_payment(check_number=...) marks PAID.
5. get_summary/export show total_paid far above contract.
findings.remediation: Reject invoices where gross+prior > contract_amount (or committed). Require status==APPROVED before record_payment. Optionally require lien waiver before PAID.

findings.title: Negative retention_percent inflates net payment to 1.5× gross
findings.description: add_subcontractor accepts any retention_percent. record_invoice computes retention = gross * retention_percent and net = gross - retention. A negative percent yields negative retention_held and net > gross.
findings.impact: PoC: retention_percent=-0.5 on $100k gross → retention_held=-$50k, amount=$150k net due.
findings.attack_path:
1. add_subcontractor(..., retention_percent=-0.5).
2. record_invoice(gross_amount=100000).
3. approve/record_payment pays $150k for $100k invoice.
findings.remediation: Clamp retention_percent to [0, 1]. Assert retention_held >= 0 and net_amount <= gross_amount.

findings.title: record_settlement from DRAFT forges SETTLED award with arbitrary amount/time
findings.description: record_settlement does not require SUBMITTED/NEGOTIATING and does not validate amount_awarded against cost_claimed or notice compliance. Any DRAFT claim becomes SETTLED with attacker-chosen dollars and days.
findings.impact: PoC: create_claim DRAFT → record_settlement(time=120, amount=2500000) → SETTLED $2.5M / 120 days with no evidence package or notice.
findings.attack_path:
1. create_claim leaves status=DRAFT.
2. Skip notices, evidence, damages, submit_claim.
3. record_settlement(claim_id, 120, 2500000).
4. generate_claim_package/status reports show settled award used for change orders/time extensions.
findings.remediation: Allow settlement only from SUBMITTED/NEGOTIATING. Cap amount_awarded <= cost_claimed unless executive override. Require notice deadlines satisfied or documented waiver.

findings.title: add_damage_calculation after SUBMITTED silently inflates cost_claimed
findings.description: add_damage_calculation has no status lock. After submit_claim, further damage lines still append and recompute cost_claimed, so the 'submitted' claim total grows without resubmission.
findings.impact: PoC: submit with $100k claimed → add $900k phantom damage → cost_claimed=$1M while status remains SUBMITTED.
findings.attack_path:
1. add_damage_calculation($100k); submit_claim.
2. add_damage_calculation($900k) still allowed.
3. Packages/settlement talks use inflated cost_claimed under SUBMITTED status.
findings.remediation: Freeze damage_calculations once status is SUBMITTED/SETTLED/WITHDRAWN; require reopen-to-DRAFT workflow to amend.

findings.title: Negative retainage_percent credits the pay app — $500k work → $750k current_payment_due
findings.description: Constructor sets retainage_percent from caller with no bounds. retainage_amount = total_completed_to_date * retainage_percent; negative percent makes retainage_held negative and current_payment_due exceed earned work. Parallel class to curated processor retainage bug; different skill/API.
findings.attack_path:
1. PaymentApplicationGenerator(..., retainage=-0.5).
2. setup_sov + create_application with full work progress.
3. calculate_payment_due / generate_g702 emit inflated payment.
findings.remediation: Clamp retainage to [0, 1]; assert retainage_amount >= 0 in calculate_payment_due.

findings.title: adjust_budget has no approval gate — unauthenticated +$100k revision erases critical overrun
findings.description: adjust_budget adds any amount to current_budget with only a notes string. No VarianceRecord approval, no CONTINGENCY pool check (distinct from already-reported curated use_contingency). calculate_summary then reports healthier variance / contingency_used delta.
findings.impact: PoC: item budget $100k / actual $180k / forecast $180k (variance=-$80k CRITICAL) → adjust_budget(+100000) → variance=+$20k UNDER_BUDGET appearance.
findings.attack_path:
1. Costs update shows CRITICAL overrun.
2. Attacker calls adjust_budget(code, 100000, 'fake approved change').
3. Reports/export show on-track variance masking the overrun.
findings.remediation: Require linked approved change-order id / VarianceRecord.approved before budget increases. Cap adjustments to remaining contingency pool. Audit trail with authenticator.

findings.title: can_release_payment treats RECEIVED (even empty file_path) as verified — skips VERIFIED state
findings.description: receive_waiver sets status=RECEIVED for any file_path including empty string and does not require verify_waiver. can_release_payment allows release when waiver status is RECEIVED or VERIFIED and returns reason 'All waivers verified'. Distinct from already-reported convert_to_unconditional waiver_id overwrite.
findings.impact: PoC: can_release_payment False → receive_waiver(id, file_path='') → can_release True for $90k approved amount without VERIFIED and without a real waiver document.
findings.attack_path:
1. create_payment_application creates REQUESTED conditional waiver.
2. Attacker calls receive_waiver(waiver_id, file_path='').
3. _check_pay_app_waivers marks waivers_complete.
4. can_release_payment returns can_release=True with amount=amount_approved.
5. Payment released without verified lien waiver on file.
findings.remediation: Require non-empty stored artifact hash/path. Gate can_release_payment on VERIFIED only. Separate receive vs verify steps with role checks.
